extracted.intended_audience: education researchers, program evaluators, policymakers, and practitioners (teachers/administrators) interested in evaluating or implementing the 6+1 Trait Writing program
extracted.subtask_description: Estimating and interpreting the impact of the 6+1 Trait Writing intervention on grade 5 student writing achievement, including measurement of trait-specific scores, teacher implementation fidelity, and robustness/sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic overall writing quality score (1–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome measure for the confirmatory question: a score for overall writing quality on a six-point scale ranging from 1 (indicating a severely flawed essay demonstrating very little or no mastery) to 6 (indicating an essay demonstrating clear and consistent mastery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary outcome. Scores on the original scale have half-point increments. Estimated treatment effect reported as covariate-adjusted posttest score difference, with standard errors adjusted for nesting of students within schools. Effect sizes (standardized differences) and confidence intervals are reported for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas (trait scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six trait scales measuring the quality of essay 'Ideas'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trait-specific covariate-adjusted posttest scores are reported and compared between treatment and control groups. For Ideas the treatment mean exceeded the control mean but difference was not statistically significant in this study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization (trait scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six trait scales measuring 'Organization' in student writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization showed a statistically significant treatment effect (p < .05) with reported effect size (e.g., effect sizes reported in table 13). Trait-specific analyses adjust for covariates and nesting like the holistic score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (trait scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six trait scales measuring 'Voice' in student writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice showed a statistically significant treatment effect (p < .05) with a reported effect size; analyses are covariate-adjusted and account for nesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice (trait scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six trait scales measuring 'Word Choice' in student writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word Choice showed a statistically significant treatment effect (p < .05) with effect size reported (e.g., 0.132–0.144 range across tables); trait scores are covariate-adjusted and clustered SEs used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence fluency (trait scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six trait scales measuring 'Sentence Fluency'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentence Fluency had treatment group means higher than control but differences were smaller and did not reach conventional significance in the main analyses; reported p-values and effect sizes are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions (trait scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six trait scales measuring 'Conventions' (grammar, mechanics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions showed small differences favoring treatment that were not statistically significant; trait analyses follow same covariate-adjusted multilevel modeling approach as holistic score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation trait (not scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: The trait of 'Presentation' is part of the 6+1 trait framework but was not scored or analyzed because students did not have opportunity to address presentation issues during the assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly excluded from trait scoring; results and interpretations apply only to the six scored traits and holistic score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching the language of rubrics for writing assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten instructional-strategy scales measured by teacher self-report (7 survey items contributed to this scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers reported frequency/extent of this practice on a 0–6 scale; at end-of-year treatment group reported higher use (mean 4.39) than control (mean 3.02); differences were statistically significant. Note: when items referring to writing traits were removed, this scale no longer existed because all its items referred to writing traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading and scoring papers and justifying the scores
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (5 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by teacher self-report; treatment teachers reported significantly higher use at end-of-year. Scale reliability (coefficient alpha) reported for teacher scales; example coefficients provided in tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching focused revision strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (5 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment teachers reported higher use; midyear differences on this scale became non-significant when items referring to writing traits were excluded—showing sensitivity to item composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling participation in the writing process
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (4 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment teachers reported higher use; differences at midyear lost significance when trait-referenced items were removed, indicating measurement sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Having students read and analyze materials that demonstrate varying writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (3 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by teacher self-report; treatment group reported greater use at end-of-year, with statistical tests accounting for clustering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving students writing assignments to respond to effective prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (4 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported for treatment vs control; treatment higher at end-of-year; reliability and mean scores presented in tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaving writing lessons into other subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (4 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment teachers reported greater use than control; statistical significance reported with t-tests adjusted for clustering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching students to set goals and monitor their progress
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (5 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment > control at end-of-year; scale means, SDs, and test statistics provided; interpreted cautiously because measures are self-reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating learning goals for writing into curriculum planning
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (4 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment teachers reported higher use; table reports means, SDs, coefficient alpha for scales, and inferential tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching ways to structure nonfiction writing
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ten teacher instructional-strategy scales (4 survey items contributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment teachers reported higher use at end-of-year; significance tested with clustered t-tests and reported in tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total teacher practice score (mean of the 10 scale scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: An overall teacher-level implementation index calculated as the mean of the 10 instructional-strategy scale scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as average total score (range of individual scales 0–6). At end-of-year, treatment group average corresponded to 'emphasized often or strongly' (~4.06) while control was ~3.24 ('between emphasized often/strongly and emphasized somewhat'). Interpretations limited because measures are self-reported and absolute implementation level cannot be definitively determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation fidelity categories (nonimplementer; basic/advanced fidelity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher-reported categorical classification of fidelity: nonimplementer vs basic or advanced fidelity to the 6+1 Trait Writing model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported proportions at baseline, midyear, and end-of-year for treatment and control (e.g., treatment rose to 85.6% basic/advanced at end-of-year). Used to contextualize impact estimates; study did not achieve perfect contrast between implementers and nonimplementers in a large-scale effectiveness trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement via teacher self-report and mitigation of social desirability
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary data on classroom practices collected via paper self-administered surveys rather than interviewer-administered surveys, with assurances of privacy (administrators did not have access to individual answers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper surveys and privacy reduce but do not eliminate potential over- or under-reporting. No independent classroom observations were conducted to validate self-reports; possible systematic bias between experimental groups cannot be ruled out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of missing data: multiple imputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 5.5 percent of student posttest records were missing; the benchmark analysis used multiple imputation to estimate missing posttest scores before analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple imputation preserves the randomized sample and was part of the original analysis plan. Sensitivity analysis re-ran models excluding students without posttests to check robustness (results similar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covariate adjustment and matched-pair design
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact estimates adjusted for pretest scores and the matched pairing of schools (pairing based on school rates of eligibility for free or reduced-price lunch), plus school-level covariates for teacher-reported hours students spend practicing writing, teacher years of experience, and teacher years of experience teaching writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covariate adjustment yields a more accurate estimate of treatment effect. The report presents covariate-adjusted posttest predictions for treatment and control under specified referent conditions (appendix details). Sensitivity analysis also tested models without the school-level covariates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical adjustment for clustering/nesting
rubrics_metrics.description: All standard errors, t-tests, and significance tests are adjusted to reflect nesting of students within schools; t-tests were calculated accounting for clustering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multilevel modeling and clustered SEs are used throughout; tables report adjusted SEs and test statistics (z/t) and p-values reflecting clustering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect size reporting and interpretation (standardized effects / Glass's delta)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment impacts are reported as raw score differences, standardized effect sizes (e.g., 0.109), and Glass's delta (standardized difference using control group SD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect sizes are interpreted substantively (e.g., 0.11 increases average percentile from 50th to ~54th). Confidence intervals and p-values accompany effect size estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses for robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Replication analyses to test sensitivity of the benchmark finding: (1) excluding students without posttest scores (listwise deletion), and (2) removing school-level covariates from the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both sensitivity tests produced substantively similar positive significant impacts, though effect magnitude varied slightly (e.g., standardized effect sizes reported: 0.110 and 0.081). Sensitivity analyses are required to assess robustness to modeling choices and missing-data assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale reliability (coefficient alpha) for teacher/practice scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal consistency reliability reported for practice scales (e.g., coefficient alpha = 0.93 for a scale shown in table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High coefficient alpha reported for many scales supports internal consistency; reliability is reported alongside means/SDs and should be considered when interpreting scale scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring ranges and anchors for teacher/practice scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher survey scale item scores ranged from 0 to 6; mean scale scores and standard deviations are reported for treatment and control groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor interpretation provided (e.g., mean of 4.06 corresponds to 'emphasized often or strongly'). Use anchor labels to interpret substantive meaning of scale means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample inclusion/exclusion rules (applicability limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: English language learners who were pulled out of the regular classroom for specialized writing instruction were excluded from the sample; ELLs who could participate in mainstream classroom instruction were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings cannot be applied to students pulled out for specialized instruction. Missing gender/ethnicity codes were handled via imputation in subgroup analyses; sample sizes for subgroup tests are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity of measurement to item content (trait-referenced items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some survey items explicitly referred to 'writing traits'; excluding those items changed the existence/significance of some scales (e.g., 'teaching the language of rubrics' scale no longer existed when trait items were dropped).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement of implementation fidelity can be sensitive to whether items reference intervention-specific language; analysts should re-calculate scales without intervention-referent items to assess potential contamination of measures.
